description: Measurement data from the German Federal Institute of Hydrology on exhaust plumes of inland ships on the Rhine at Worms, published as a measurement report in Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics (2023). Contents: plumes of around 4,700 ship passages detected between March 2021 and June 2022, matched with automatic identification system (AIS) ship data, with NOx, NO2 and CO2 gas measurements and particle number, size distribution from 5 nm to 10 µm, PM1, PM2.5, ultrafine fraction and black carbon. One station sat in a bridge above the channel, the other on the bank 40 m from the lane, representing people living or working by the river. Results include ship contributions (7 percent of local NO2 at the bridge) and fuel-based emission factors per ship. Coverage: one Upper Rhine site, 2021-2022. Format and access: open paper with supplement; the datasets are archived under a DOI given in the paper. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo record and article). Access is free of charge. Caveats: a single site, and emission factors vary widely between ships and engine ages. Useful for hazard exposure and health impact modelling of riverside populations and for emission factors in inland fleet scenarios. It relates to the Rhine 2018 low water case study and CBS inland shipping statistics in the catalogue.
